title: Cross-lingual span alignment — scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick scratch notes on tricky cross-lingual span alignment and labeling heuristics. Mostly for myself + quick hand-off to reviewers (Liam/Sofia).

Context:
- We're getting more mixed-language sources (fr/en, es/en, zh/en) after adding international scraping.
- Current span mapping heuristics assume 1:1 token alignment and clean sentence boundaries -> fails frequently.

Common failure modes observed (examples):
1) Translation expansion/contraction
   - src (fr): "Il a donné son accord" (3 tokens) -> tgt (en): "He gave his full consent yesterday" (7 tokens plus extra context from translator).
   - Problem: label anchored to short src span ends up misaligned to long tgt span; sometimes label should cover only core phrase but translator added clarifier.
   - Heuristic idea: prefer alignments that minimize label length ratio beyond threshold (e.g., if tgt/span_length > src_length * 3, flag for human review).

2) Partial overlap due to idiomatic translation
   - src (es): "me cae bien" -> tgt (en): "I like him" (not literal). Entity/intent boundaries shift.
   - Approach: add a fuzzy token overlap metric (subsequence match after lemmatization) and if low, prefer labeling on source language only or propagate 'uncertain' flag.

3) Tokenization mismatches (Agglutinative languages / clitics)
   - pt: "diz-se" or fr clitics: "j'aime" -> tokenization splits cause different span indices.
   - Fix: store and use character-level spans as canonical mapping, not token indices. When char-span mapping impossible (no alignment), fallback to alignment via bilingual dictionary or word-level aligner.

4) Sentence split mismatch / sentence fusion
   - src had two short sentences, translator fused them into one longer sentence -> label mapping becomes ambiguous (which source sentence does label attach to?).
   - Rule: if sentence boundary counts differ, try to align at clause-level using punctuation and conjunction heuristics; if ambiguous, mark 'multi-src' and send sample to review queue.

Edge-case policy proposals (quick):
- Default: keep ground truth label attached to source language span (store both src char span and src token span) and mark propagated target mapping as 'auto-prop' with confidence score.
- Auto-propagation threshold: only propagate if alignment score > 0.7 AND length_ratio between 0.5 and 2.5. Otherwise label as 'needs-review'.
- For translations that add context (temporal words, clarifiers): try to detect adverbial/temporal insertions via POS tags and exclude them from propagated label (i.e., align core head phrase).

Quick heuristics / scoring ideas (for pipeline):
- Alignment score = 0.6 * (char overlap normalized) + 0.3 * (word embedding cosine of phrase embedding) + 0.1 * (bilingual dictionary coverage)
- Penalize if additional tokens in target are outside punctuation boundaries and not present in bilingual dict -> low confidence.

Examples from dataset (hand-picked) — format: src | src_span | tgt | observed mapping problem
- "es: La CAI aprobó la medida" | span: "la medida" -> en: "The committee approved the measure yesterday after debate" | target span diffuses across phrase + time adverb -> label inflated.
- "fr: le patient présente une fièvre" | span: "fièvre" -> en: "the patient is running a fever and seems disoriented" | english adds symptom cluster, mapping unclear (label should still be "fever").

Annotation UI suggestions for quick triage:
- Show source and target side-by-side with char-level hover highlighting.
- Slider to accept/adjust propagated span on target, with suggested 'confidence' (auto-filled).
- Single-click tag: Accept/Adjust/Reject propagation -> quick metrics to tune thresholds.

Sampling strategy for review queue:
- Always sample: low-confidence auto-propagations (score < 0.7), length_ratio > 2.0, added temporal/adverb tokens detected.
- Also sample random 1% of high-confidence wins to monitor precision drift.

Label guideline draft snippets (to include in final doc):
- "When in doubt, keep source-labeled span as canonical ground truth; propagated target spans should be used only to assist model training if accepted by a human reviewer."
- "If a propagated target span contains added clarifying words not present in source, trim propagation to core phrase unless meaning changes."

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Run a quick alignment experiment on 1k bilingual pairs using fast-align or eflomal to compute distribution of length_ratio and alignment scores. (assign -> Liam)
- Add character-span storage to export format (we currently only store token indices). Technical ticket needed. (assign -> Eng infra)
- Define final numeric thresholds after above experiment and pilot UI. (assign -> me + Sofia)

Notes-to-self: keep this fuzzy — want to capture examples in raw form, then formalize into labeling doc. Add more multilingual examples (zh, ru) next pass.

-- end scratchpad --
